lens: human-first handling of candidate evidence, respectful interpretation, transparency, restraint, and reversible recruiter action

findings.observation: The reviewed surfaces label the source as synthetic, preserve exact evidence, and require a separate Submit, but this run still has no user Google Chrome recording of the toolbar or selected-text gesture and temporary activeTab grant.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/round-2/final/chrome-manual-gap.json records the absent visible chrome://extensions, toolbar, and positive activeTab evidence; docs/evaluations/round-2/browser-extension/01-core-review-390.png shows only the reviewed extension package state.
findings.user_impact: The downstream workflow is restrained, but the run cannot prove that a candidate conversation enters it only through the promised deliberate recruiter gesture.
findings.recommendation: Repeat the exact package digest in a policy-authorized user Google Chrome profile and keep the exact selected evidence visible until explicit Submit.
findings.verification: A direct recording shows a synthetic source, visible toolbar or selected-text invocation, exact evidence preview, explicit Submit, and no earlier transfer.

strengths: The system records evidence-backed situational facts and never ranks candidate worth, personality, protected traits, culture fit, or acceptance probability.
Exact evidence, proposed facts, recruiter decisions, action authority, and observed outcome remain visibly distinct.
No candidate contact, calendar, message, ATS, CRM, or other external write was attempted.
No-action and ambiguity fixtures prevent manufactured urgency and unsupported interpretation.
missing_evidence: Direct user Google Chrome capture-permission and review recording.
Candidate-facing notice, consent, and retention policy evaluation remains outside this synthetic recruiter-only slice.
open_questions: What notice and deletion route will a live product expose before any real conversation can be submitted?
